body.statement:
Put \(D=Sd\).  The class \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)\) is empty when \(B<D^2\).  For each fixed nonempty class with donor-envelope interior compatibility \(B>D^2\), and each \(q\in\{\mathrm{tr},\mathrm{sm},\mathrm{sp},\mathrm{don}\}\), there are pairs
\[
(P_{0,q},P_{1,q})\subset
\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)
\]
such that \(P_{\ell,q}(z_0\in\mathcal Z_+\mid E_0)\ge c_X\), their conditional joint observed-data testing affinity is uniformly bounded away from zero,
\[
\inf_{N,T,\mathbf n}\int\min\{dP_{0,q},dP_{1,q}\}>0,
\]
and
\[
|\tau_{n,P_{1,q}}(z_0)-\tau_{n,P_{0,q}}(z_0)|^2
\ge cR_q
\quad\text{on }\mathcal Z_+,
\]
where \(R_q\) uses \(R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\) in the spacing channel.  The constants in the donor pair may depend on the fixed slack \(B-D^2\).  The treated-mean, replicated-smoothing, and donor pairs may additionally be chosen with uniformly bounded Kullback--Leibler divergence; for the random-spacing pair only positive testing affinity is asserted.  For each fixed otherwise nonempty boundary class with \(B=D^2\), the same assertions hold for \(q\in\{\mathrm{tr},\mathrm{sm},\mathrm{sp}\}\), using one common donor marginal, but no universal donor-channel pair or \(R_{\mathrm{don}}\) converse is asserted.  Every asserted pair is induced by a regular conditional law of the complete causal panel; in particular, its event means are stable given the complete historical design and its historical errors are centered given that design.
body.justification: All four pairs are completed as causal panels for fixed \(B>D^2\); the equality boundary retains the treated, smoothing, and spacing pairs with one common donor marginal.
body.gap: The finite common-support donor mean perturbation needs fixed fourth-moment slack, whereas nonemptiness alone supplies only \(B\ge D^2\).
body.consumer: The two frontier theorems use four lower channels under strict slack and exactly three at equality.
body.proof_tex:
Fix a regular conditional experiment given \(E_0\), put \(D=Sd\), and, for any class member, define the proof variable
\[
Y=\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_1-z_0).
\]
The definitions of \(z_0\) and \(\Sigma\), together with positive definiteness in \texttt{ass:donor-ellipticity}, give
\[
\mathbb E_P[YY^\top\mid E_0]=I_D.
\]
Taking traces and then applying Jensen's inequality to the nonnegative variable \(\|Y\|_2^2\) yields
\[
\mathbb E_P[\|Y\|_2^2\mid E_0]=\operatorname{tr}(I_D)=D,
\qquad
D^2\le \mathbb E_P[\|Y\|_2^4\mid E_0]\le B.
\tag{1}
\]
The final inequality is exactly \texttt{ass:donor-fourth-moment}.  Hence \(B\ge D^2\) is necessary for nonemptiness; the class is empty if \(B<D^2\).  Notice that strict inequality is not a consequence of nonemptiness.

We next give a causal completion used in every asserted channel.  Let
\[
\mathscr X=\sigma\{X_{st}:1\le s\le S,\ 1\le t\le T\}.
\]
Choose the event path in a fixed compact subset of \(\mathcal Z_+\) contained in the interior of \(([0,1]^d)^S\).  All Bernoulli response probabilities below are kept in a fixed interval \([\eta,1-\eta]\), where \(0<\eta<1/2\), and the corresponding responses take values in \(\{0,B\}\).  For \(p,p+v\in[\eta,1-\eta]\), two differentiations of binary relative entropy, whose second derivative is bounded on this interval, give
\[
\operatorname{kl}(p+v,p)\le C_\eta v^2.
\tag{2}
\]
Draw event outcomes independently of \(\mathscr X\).  Conditional on \(\mathscr X\), draw bounded historical response paths independently across \((s,i)\), from kernels which may vary with \((s,i)\) but satisfy
\[
\mathbb E_P[Q_{sti}\mid\mathscr X,E_0]=m_s(X_{st}).
\]
Thus, with \(\varepsilon_{sti}=Q_{sti}-m_s(X_{st})\),
\[
\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathscr X,E_0]
=\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid E_0],
\qquad
\mathbb E_P[\varepsilon_{sti}\mid\mathscr X,E_0]=0.
\tag{3}
\]
Complete the unobserved event-date untreated potential outcomes so that their cohort-average conditional means equal \(m_s(z_{0s})\).  Set the observed and historical potential outcomes according to \texttt{ass:consistency} and \texttt{ass:historical-consistency}; make historical potential outcomes invariant to event treatment and every potential outcome invariant to other units' assignments.  These choices give limited anticipation, no spillovers, event transport, and the two full-design restrictions in \texttt{def:full-design-centered-class}.  Set \(X_{st}^{\mathrm{obs}}=X_{st}\).  In each construction the donor sample is conditionally iid, independent of the panel, and satisfies the covariance and moment envelopes.  Thus the construction is a regular conditional causal-panel law rather than merely an observed regression experiment.

For every compatible \(B\ge D^2\), the three non-donor channels can use the same common donor marginal.  Conditional on \(E_0\), let \(U\) be uniform on
\[
\{\pm\sqrt D\,e_k:1\le k\le D\},
\qquad Z_j=z_0+U_j,
\]
with the \(U_j\)'s iid and independent of the panel.  Symmetry gives
\[
\mathbb E[U\mid E_0]=0,
\qquad
\mathbb E[UU^\top\mid E_0]=I_D,
\qquad
\mathbb E[\|U\|_2^4\mid E_0]=D^2\le B.
\tag{4}
\]
Because \(c_\Sigma\le1\le C_\Sigma\), (4) verifies both donor envelopes even at \(B=D^2\).

For the treated channel, put
\[
V_{\mathrm{tr}}=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}=R_{\mathrm{tr}},
\qquad
v_s=c_0\frac{\pi_s}{n_sV_{\mathrm{tr}}^{1/2}}.
\]
Since \(V_{\mathrm{tr}}\ge\pi_s^2/n_s\), \(|v_s|\le c_0n_s^{-1/2}\le c_0\).  A sufficiently small fixed \(c_0\) keeps every event-response probability in \([\eta,1-\eta]\).  Change only the treated event-response probability in cohort \(s\) by \(v_s\).  The untreated surfaces and all other observed laws remain fixed.  Absorbing the fixed wealth scale into constants, \texttt{lem:identification-fwl} and (2) give
\[
|\tau_{n,P_{1,\mathrm{tr}}}(z_0)-
\tau_{n,P_{0,\mathrm{tr}}}(z_0)|
=c_0V_{\mathrm{tr}}^{1/2},
\qquad
\operatorname{KL}(P_{1,\mathrm{tr}},P_{0,\mathrm{tr}})
\le C\sum_s n_sv_s^2\le Cc_0^2.
\tag{5}
\]

For the smoothing channel, choose \(s_*\) maximizing
\(\pi_s^2(Tn_s)^{-2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}\) and set
\[
b=c_b(Tn_{s_*})^{-1/(2\lambda+d)},
\]
where fixed \(c_b>0\) is small enough that the bump support stays in the interior cube for all positive sample sizes.  Perturb only this cohort by
\[
m_{s_*,1}(x)-m_{s_*,0}(x)
=c_1b^\lambda\psi((x-z_{0s_*})/b),
\tag{6}
\]
where \(\psi\) is a fixed smooth compactly supported bump with \(\psi(0)=1\).  Use an affine carrier having nonzero covariance-standardized slope when \(\lambda>1\), and an asymmetric \(\lambda\)-cusp carrier when \(0<\lambda\le1\), scaled within the response, Holder, and two-sided-modulus envelopes.  For \(\delta\le b\), the increment of (6) over a displacement of length \(\delta\) is at most \(Cc_1\delta^\kappa\) by Holder continuity (and the derivative bound when \(\lambda>1\)); for \(\delta>b\), boundedness of the bump and \(b^\lambda\le C\delta^\kappa\) gives the same conclusion.  Hence sufficiently small fixed \(c_1\) preserves both sides of the local-modulus condition.  Because \(S\) is fixed,
\[
\begin{aligned}
|\tau_{n,P_{1,\mathrm{sm}}}(z_0)-
\tau_{n,P_{0,\mathrm{sm}}}(z_0)|^2
&=c_1^2\pi_{s_*}^2b^{2\lambda}\\
&\ge c\sum_s\pi_s^2(Tn_s)^{-2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}
=cR_{\mathrm{sm}}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{7}
\]
Use an independent uniform historical design.  Its probability of meeting the bump support is at most \(Cb^d\).  Conditional product structure, (2), and integration over the design yield
\[
\operatorname{KL}(P_{1,\mathrm{sm}},P_{0,\mathrm{sm}})
\le CTn_{s_*}b^{2\lambda+d}\le C.
\tag{8}
\]

For the spacing channel use \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-spacing-obstruction}, whose construction uses the common marginal (4).  It gives
\[
\int\min\{dP_{0,\mathrm{sp}},dP_{1,\mathrm{sp}}\}
\ge a_{\mathrm{sp}}>0,
\qquad
|\tau_{n,P_{1,\mathrm{sp}}}(z_0)-
\tau_{n,P_{0,\mathrm{sp}}}(z_0)|^2
\ge cR_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}.
\tag{9}
\]
Only positive affinity is used.  The rare-active-block probability in that construction may be decreased by a fixed factor, making the affinity exceed any prescribed number below one while retaining the rate in (9).

It remains to construct the donor channel, for which we now impose the fixed strict slack \(B-D^2>0\).  Choose \(0<\xi<D\) so that
\[
D^2+\xi^2<B,
\]
put \(r_-=(D-\xi)^{1/2}\) and \(r_+=(D+\xi)^{1/2}\), and choose two interior centers
\[
z^{(1)}=z^{(0)}+\mu e_1,
\qquad \mu=c_2N^{-1/2}.
\]
The direction \(e_1\) is chosen inside one cohort block.  Use the common finite support
\[
\mathcal A=\{z^{(0)}\pm r_-e_k, z^{(0)}\pm r_+e_k:1\le k\le D\}.
\]
Under law zero, give every atom probability \(1/(4D)\).  Its mean is \(z^{(0)}\), covariance is \(I_D\), and its standardized fourth moment is
\[
\frac{r_-^4+r_+^4}{2}=D^2+\xi^2<B.
\tag{10}
\]
Under law one leave all probabilities except the four atoms in direction \(e_1\) unchanged.  With
\[
a_N=\frac{\mu}{2r_-},
\qquad b_N=\frac{\mu^2}{2\xi},
\]
replace the probabilities at \(z^{(0)}+r_-e_1\), \(z^{(0)}-r_-e_1\), \(z^{(0)}+r_+e_1\), and \(z^{(0)}-r_+e_1\), respectively, by
\[
\frac1{4D}-\frac{b_N}{2}+a_N,
\quad
\frac1{4D}-\frac{b_N}{2}-a_N,
\quad
\frac1{4D}+\frac{b_N}{2},
\quad
\frac1{4D}+\frac{b_N}{2}.
\tag{11}
\]
For sufficiently small fixed \(c_2\), depending on the fixed slack through \(\xi\), all probabilities in (11) are positive for every \(N\).  They sum to their baseline total.  Direct calculation gives
\[
\mathbb E_1[Z_j-z^{(0)}]=2a_Nr_-e_1=\mu e_1,
\]
and
\[
\mathbb E_1[(Z_j-z^{(0)})(Z_j-z^{(0)})^\top]
=I_D+b_N(r_+^2-r_-^2)e_1e_1^\top
=I_D+\mu^2e_1e_1^\top.
\]
Thus \(\mathbb E_1 Z_j=z^{(1)}\) and \(\operatorname{Var}_1(Z_j\mid E_0)=I_D\), exactly.  The standardized fourth moment is a continuous function of the finite probability vector and of \(\mu\); by (10), the fixed strict slack permits a further reduction of \(c_2\) such that it remains below \(B\) under both laws.  This is the only point where \(B>D^2\), rather than mere compatibility, is used.

Since the baseline probabilities are bounded below and the perturbations in (11) are \(O(\mu)\), Taylor's formula for the finite probability-vector likelihood gives
\[
\operatorname{KL}(P_{1,\mathrm{don}},P_{0,\mathrm{don}})
\le CN(a_N^2+b_N^2)
\le CN\mu^2\le Cc_2^2.
\tag{12}
\]
For \(\kappa=1\), choose the weighted regression carrier to have nonzero linear slope in direction \(e_1\).  For \(0<\kappa=\lambda<1\), in the selected cohort use
\[
x\longmapsto c_3+c_4|e_1^\top(x-z^{(0)})|^\lambda
+c_5|e_1^\top(x-z^{(1)})|^\lambda,
\qquad c_4,c_5>0,quad c_4\ne c_5.
\tag{13}
\]
Fixed rescaling places (13) inside the response and Holder envelopes.  At \(z^{(0)}\), displacement in the direction away from \(z^{(1)}\) increases both cusp terms; at \(z^{(1)}\), displacement in the opposite outward direction does the same.  The upper Holder inequality controls every displacement.  Thus the two-sided modulus holds at both centers, while evaluation at the centers gives
\[
\left|\sum_s\pi_s\{m_s(z_s^{(1)})-m_s(z_s^{(0)})\}\right|
\ge c\mu^\kappa=cN^{-\kappa/2}.
\tag{14}
\]
Keep the historical observed law, the common regression surface, and the observed event mean fixed across the two donor laws.  Under law \(\ell\), complete untreated event outcomes with cohort means \(m_s(z_s^{(\ell)})\).  The identifying equality in \texttt{lem:identification-fwl} turns (14) into squared target separation at least \(cN^{-\kappa}=cR_{\mathrm{don}}\).

For the three bounded-divergence channels, the elementary inequality
\[
\|P_1-P_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
\le\{\operatorname{KL}(P_1,P_0)/2\}^{1/2}
\]
follows by applying data processing to the set \(\{dP_1/dP_0\ge1\}\) and bounding the resulting binary relative entropy by twice squared probability difference.  Hence
\[
\int\min\{dP_0,dP_1\}
=1-\|P_1-P_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
\ge1-\{\operatorname{KL}(P_1,P_0)/2\}^{1/2}.
\tag{15}
\]
Reducing \(c_0,c_1,c_2\) makes (15) uniformly positive for the treated, smoothing, and, only under strict slack, donor pairs; (9) handles spacing.  The chosen query belongs to \(\mathcal Z_+\) with conditional probability one.  Equations (2)--(15), the causal completion following (3), and the channelwise design, smoothness, donor, and modulus checks prove all four assertions when \(B>D^2\).  When \(B=D^2\), equations (4)--(9) prove exactly the asserted treated, smoothing, and spacing claims, without a donor converse.
